name: San José
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching San José: Costa Rican counterparty checks, real estate ownership research, services and free zone diligence.
hero_lede: San José is Costa Rica's capital and the centre of a metropolitan area holding most of the country's formal businesses, financial institutions and courts. TDSC scopes San José matters around counterparty and ownership research, real estate and fraud inquiries, and support for litigation and arbitration seated in the capital.
intro: San José is the capital of Costa Rica and the core of the Greater Metropolitan Area (Gran Área Metropolitana, GAM), which INEC census data put at about 3.1 million people, roughly 60 percent of the national population, in 2011. The canton of San José itself had an estimated 352,000 residents in 2024, while San José province had about 1.66 million. The canton concentrates finance, government, commerce and professional services: a Colegio de Ciencias Económicas study of central bank data found it alone held 14 percent of the country's registered formal businesses, and 89 percent of formal businesses nationally are in services. In the 2024 cantonal competitiveness index published by the University of Costa Rica, San José ranked third of all cantons, with the highest density of financial entities.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to San José because decisions about Costa Rican counterparties, property and disputes are usually made, registered and litigated there. Multinationals operating shared-service, medical device and technology operations in the free zones around the capital need diligence on local partners, landlords and suppliers. Investors in tourism and residential real estate need to know who stands behind sociedades anónimas holding land. Lenders and creditors pursue debtors whose assets sit in companies and properties registered in the capital. Fraud schemes involving investment offers, cross-border payments and impersonation of Costa Rican entities also bring foreign victims and their counsel to the city's courts, prosecutors and arbitration centres.

matters.title: Counterparty checks on sociedades anónimas
matters.text: Researching Costa Rican companies proposed as distributors, joint venture partners or service providers, including legal representatives, registered capital and filing history at the Registro Nacional, litigation, adverse media and links between companies sharing representatives or addresses, to identify the people who actually control them.

matters.title: Real estate ownership and title history
matters.text: Tracing ownership and encumbrances of land and buildings held through companies by investors and developers, using the national property registry, company records and litigation, to test seller claims and identify competing interests before purchase, lending or enforcement against Costa Rican property.

matters.title: Investment and payment fraud tracing
matters.text: Supporting foreign victims and counsel where funds were sent to Costa Rican companies or accounts in investment offers, online trading or impersonation schemes, by mapping entities, representatives and related parties so counsel can assess criminal complaints, precautionary measures and civil recovery.

matters.title: Free zone supplier and landlord diligence
matters.text: Checking local landlords, contractors, staffing and logistics providers that serve multinational operations in the GAM's free zones, for ownership, conflicts with client employees, tax or labour disputes and adverse media, before contracts are awarded or renewed.

matters.title: Asset research for creditors
matters.text: Identifying property, vehicles and company interests registered in Costa Rica to debtors or award respondents, through the Registro Nacional's real and movable property and companies records and court filings, so counsel can plan enforcement before courts sitting in San José.

local_context.title: Courts in the capital
local_context.text: San José is the seat of the Judicial Branch, including the Supreme Court of Justice and its First Chamber, which hears civil and commercial cassation, and the Constitutional Chamber. First-instance civil courts and appellate tribunals for the capital also sit in the city, as do the specialised prosecutor's offices handling economic crime. Civil cases follow the oral, hearing-based procedure of the 2018 Civil Procedure Code.

local_context.title: Arbitration centres
local_context.text: The main commercial arbitration institutions are based in San José. The Centro Internacional de Conciliación y Arbitraje (CICA) of AmCham Costa Rica offers arbitration, conciliation and mediation, with its council re-elected for 2025 to 2027. The Centro de Conciliación y Arbitraje of the Cámara de Comercio de Costa Rica (CCA) is the other established institution. Factual research supports claimants and respondents in either.

local_context.title: National registries in San José
local_context.text: The Registro Nacional, which keeps the companies, real property and movable property registries for the whole country, is headquartered in the capital and offers online consultation. Because registration is national, a San José search covers companies and property anywhere in Costa Rica. Shareholder information is not in the public companies register and is held separately for authorities. Searches also show liens, mortgages and annotations that matter to buyers and creditors.

local_context.title: Financial regulators
local_context.text: Costa Rica's financial supervisors, including the Superintendencia General de Entidades Financieras (SUGEF) and the securities superintendency (SUGEVAL) under the national supervisory council CONASSIF, and the central bank, are located in San José, as is the Bolsa Nacional de Valores. Licensing and sanctions information they publish is a useful check on financial counterparties claiming to be regulated. Unregistered entities offering investments should be treated with caution.

tdsc_approach: TDSC handles San José matters from Nashville and has no office or staff in Costa Rica. Engagements begin with what the client needs to decide and a review of the sources that apply: Registro Nacional company, property and movable property records, court and judicial publications, regulator lists from SUGEF and SUGEVAL, and Spanish-language media and open sources. Because shareholder records are not public, ownership conclusions are drawn carefully and labelled with their confidence. Where enquiries, interviews or site visits in the GAM are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified local professionals and agrees the approach with the client's Costa Rican counsel. Personal data is handled under Costa Rica's data protection law, and reports separate facts from inference.

faqs.q: Can the shareholders of a San José company be identified?
faqs.a: Only in part from public sources. The Registro Nacional shows legal representatives, capital, by-laws and filings, but shareholder information is reported to a separate register available to authorities rather than the public. TDSC therefore works from representatives, related companies, property, litigation and media to identify likely controllers, and states the limits clearly.

faqs.q: Where are arbitrations involving Costa Rican companies usually seated?
faqs.a: Most institutional commercial arbitrations in Costa Rica are administered in San José, mainly by CICA of AmCham Costa Rica or the CCA of the Cámara de Comercio de Costa Rica, depending on the contract clause. TDSC supports counsel in either with research on parties, witnesses, related entities and assets relevant to claims and enforcement.

faqs.q: Can property title in Costa Rica be checked before purchase?
faqs.a: Yes. The Registro Nacional records ownership, mortgages, liens and annotations for registered real property nationwide and can be consulted online. TDSC combines that with company research on corporate owners, litigation and media to test seller claims. Title opinions, survey questions and maritime zone concessions remain matters for Costa Rican counsel and surveyors.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have investigators in San José?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or licence in Costa Rica. Registry, court and open-source research is carried out from Nashville. Where local enquiries, interviews or site visits are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified Costa Rican professionals working to a written scope agreed with the client and its local counsel.

faqs.q: How can we check whether a Costa Rican firm is a regulated financial entity?
faqs.a: Compare its claims with lists and announcements published by SUGEF, SUGEVAL and the other superintendencies under CONASSIF, which are based in San José, and with the Registro Nacional's company records. Inconsistent names, recent incorporation or representatives linked to other failed ventures are warning signs that warrant fuller research before funds move.
